items.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released!
items.summary: November 19, 2026 - The PostgreSQL Global Development Grouptoday announced the release of PostgreSQL 19,the latest version of the world's most advanced open source database.Mission-critical usage of PostgreSQL continues to rapidly rise, andPostgreSQL 19 responds to this by simplifying both administration anddevelopment for these workloads at scale. This release introduces theREPACK (CONCURRENTLY)command so users can optimize tables for their current workload withoutdisruption to ongoing operations. PostgreSQL 19 gives users better control overplan stability and query performance with the new pg_plan_adviceextension. Developers will find many delightful features in this release, fromsupport for "read-your-writes" consistency on standbys to "get or create"behavior that saves a network round trip."For over 30 years, the global open source community has built PostgreSQL into adatabase that organizations trust with their most critical data," saidJonathan Katz, a member of the PostgreSQL core team. "PostgreSQL 19 continuesthat commitment to reliability, giving users new ways to manage their workloadswithout disruption and to build applications that span multiple systems."PostgreSQL, an innovative data management system known for its reliability,robustness, and extensibility, benefits from 30 years of open sourcedevelopment from a global developer community and has become the preferred opensource relational database for organizations of all sizes.Simplifying workload managementTables that receive many updates and deletes can build up unused space, known as"bloat," which can also significantly impact query performance. TheVACUUM FULL and CLUSTER commands were previously used to handle this, buthad tradeoffs, including preventing access to the table until the cleanupfinished. PostgreSQL 19 introduces the REPACKcommand, which reclaims this space and can reorder a table's data to match anindex, and with REPACK (CONCURRENTLY), can do so without blocking reads orwrites. REPACK replaces the VACUUM FULL and CLUSTER commands, both ofwhich remain available for compatibility.The PostgreSQL query planner usually picks an efficient plan for each query, butthe plan can change as your data changes, and sometimes the new plan is slower.PostgreSQL 19 adds the pg_plan_adviceextension, which allows stabilization of plan choices and the ability toexperiment with different plans using the "plan advice" mini-language. The companionpg_stash_adviceextension stores advice and automatically applies it to queries based on theirquery identifier, so you can fix a slow plan without changing your application.PostgreSQL 19 also helps autovacuumkeep up on busy systems. Autovacuum can now vacuum indexes using parallelworkers, controlled by the newautovacuum_max_parallel_workerssetting, and uses a new scoring systemto decide which tables to process first. Queries that read a table can nowautomatically mark pages as all-visible in the visibility map during execution,reducing the work that future vacuums need to do. Additionally,vacuumdb --analyze-onlynow analyzes partitioned tables when no tables are specified.This release adds new views for monitoring workloads, includingpg_stat_lockfor per-lock-type statistics, pg_stat_recoveryfor recovery status, and pg_stat_autovacuum_scoresto show how autovacuum prioritizes tables. The new IO option forEXPLAIN ANALYZE and thematching auto_explainsetting report asynchronous I/O activity. PostgreSQL 19 also reports the amountof WAL written for full-page images in pg_stat_wal,EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, WAL), and in vacuum and analyze log events.Distributed data improvementsPreviously, PostgreSQL often required users to restart their server to enablelogical replication,which could be disruptive in production workloads. PostgreSQL 19 simplifieslogical replication initialization by automatically raising the effective WALlevel to logical when you create the first logical replication slot. You cansee the WAL level in use with the new effective_wal_level setting.PostgreSQL 19 also adds logical replication ofsequence values,which you can publish using FOR ALL SEQUENCES withCREATE PUBLICATION.CREATE PUBLICATION also adds an EXCEPT clause to exclude tables whenpublishing FOR ALL TABLES, and CREATE SUBSCRIPTIONcan now get its connection settings from a foreign server, such as one definedwith postgres_fdw,using the SERVER clause. Additionally, the newretain_dead_tuplessubscription option lets PostgreSQL detect updates that conflict with aconcurrent delete, and these conflicts are counted inpg_stat_subscription_stats.For applications that send reads to standbys, PostgreSQL 19 adds"read-your-writes" consistency with the newWAIT FOR LSN command. Asession on a standby can use WAIT FOR LSN to wait until the standby hasreplayed the write-ahead log (WAL) up to a specificlog sequence number (LSN)before running a query, so the application can read data it just wrote on theprimary.PostgreSQL 19 also improves queries on foreign tables.
